record.disposition:
DISPOSITION 
•
Internal medicine referral 
•
Will likely require ICU/High care 
•
Continue serial ECG and VBG monitoring in ED 
ISONIAZID (INH) OVERDOSE 
 
GENERAL APPROACH 
Consider INH toxicity in all refractory seizures, especially if on TB Rx/prophylaxis 
• 
Clinical features: Depletes Vit B6, causing decreased GABA – seizures, lactic acidosis 
• 
ECG Features: No specific features, sinus tachycardia 
• 
Blood gas: HAGMA, severe lactic acidosis 
• 
Triage to RESUS AREA, even if patient initially appears well 
• 
Terminate seizures with Benzodiazepines (high doses may be required). 
See Status Epilepticus protocol, but avoid anti-epileptic agents. 
• 
Rapid ABC assessment, 2 IV lines, monitors, HGT, VBG, urine ßHCG, ECG 
• 
Early airway management – will require intubation prior to Pyridoxine administration 
• 
Correct abnormal electrolytes, consider other causes of seizures 
• 
Crystalloid fluid bolus 20mg/kg if hypotensive 
• 
Comprehensive history and exam, including:
